messages.subject: Increase bounded memory limit
parts:
Hi Henrik,

Aroma.affymetrix processes data sets in bounded memory, which is a
great quality. But I'm wondering is there is a way to change that
amount of memory, in order to take advantage of a system where a lot
of RAM is available, for example.

Thank you so much!
Nicolas

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Increase bounded memory limit
parts:
On Tue, May 20, 2008 at 3:20 PM, Nicolas Stransky
<nicolas....@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
>
> Aroma.affymetrix processes data sets in bounded memory, which is a
> great quality. But I'm wondering is there is a way to change that
> amount of memory, in order to take advantage of a system where a lot
> of RAM is available, for example.

this mostly makes sense for methods processing data in "chunks", such
as the ProbeLevelModel classes. The fit() function for these takes
the argument 'ram', which is a scale factor that defaults to one, but
if you set ram > 1 you will use more memory per chunk and vice versa.
This will speed up the fitting a bit but at that the improvement will
be less the large value you use. Turn on 'verbose' (verbose=-10) and
you'll see how much time fit() spends on read and write compared to
actual fitting.

If you're looking for ways to speed up analysis on GWS5 and GWS6, it's
been discussed before in thread 'Parallelizing the Total Copy Number
Analysis (GWS6)', in which I outline some immediate improvements that
will speed up fit() for chips with single-probe units. Again, these
things are on the todo/wishlist but are not likely to be implemented
anytime soon.

Cheers

Henrik

Thanks, that's right, I remember asking how to possibly parallelize
the CN analysis. And if I remember correctly, you also said that the
same data was read and overwritten several times because of the
current implementation. This is why I thought that increasing the
chunk size could decrease the amount of data to be written and thus,
decrease the time spent on read/write. Maybe I'm wrong.

all the files that aroma.affymetrix uses or generates stay in the
filesystem cache and so, the harddrive or network access is not the
bottleneck. This is a general consideration, though.
